target_name: Broad Sample Worst Year Charge Coverage
rationale: A defensible consolidation of two independently validated design choices (downside-tail cash input and the COALESCE sample extension) that carries a distinct economic claim about bad-year autonomy rather than a pure rescaling, though it remains an incremental merge of archive variants and inherits the family's implicit double-count of interest (oancf is already net of interest paid).

target_name: Surplus After Commitments And Asset Replacement
rationale: Deducting depreciation as a maintenance claim is genuinely new economic content for this family, but note that oancf minus dp collapses toward accrual earnings, so the signal risks partially reducing to a standard earnings-to-assets profitability measure rather than isolating discretionary surplus.

target_name: Market Dependence Per Unit Of Internal Capacity
rationale: Issuance deflated by internal cash capacity is close to a monotone re-expression of the already-tested "Internal Funding Share Of Total Capital" (both are essentially functions of issuance/|oancf|), and it also sits squarely on top of the published net-external-financing anomaly, so the only difference is the addition of xint+dvt to the denominator — a cosmetic change.

target_name: Consolidated Autonomy And Capital Return Score
rationale: A coherent three-leg composite of separately validated channels, but it is close to a kitchen-sink assembly of archive winners with an unacknowledged implicit weighting (nesting gives coverage 50% and each other leg 25%), so any improvement will be hard to attribute and prone to archive-fitting.

This is the archive's "Persistent Fixed Charge Coverage Regime" with the input series swapped for the already-tested COALESCE variant — a pure sample-extension rediscovery with no new economic content, and it duplicates the same tweak proposed in Signal 1.

target_name: Coverage Of Recurring And Maturing Claims
rationale: The union of recurring charges and maturing principal has not in fact been evaluated and the test question is well posed, though the construct mixes a stock (dlc) with flows and is likely to load heavily on a short-debt/leverage tilt already captured by the two parent signals.
